mutations.because: fromBrief must coalesce a D68-legal null targetAudience to an empty string. Dropping ?? "" copies null through and validateIdentity throws on .trim() instead of reporting the empty-audience error.
command: a null targetAudience is an identity error, not a throw

mutations.because: Spreading the product over emptyProduct lets name: null overwrite the default. Without the per-field ?? "", validateProducts throws on product.name.trim() instead of reporting the product-name error.
command: a product with a null name is a product-name error, not a throw

mutations.because: canonicalBrief must map a null targetAudience to "" so the snapshot matches toBrief. Leaving the raw null in the snapshot makes a freshly opened file read dirty only because null became "". (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: the recorded text was reformatted or moved, not changed — the after-text is re-wrapped the same way, and the edit it encodes, the claim and the command are untouched.)
command: a freshly opened brief with a null scalar is not dirty

mutations.because: canonicalNullScalars runs on the unvalidated stored snapshot in normalizeDraftState. Without the Array.isArray guard a stored products: null throws, the draft cannot be recovered, and loadDraftFromStorage discards the whole file.
command: a stored draft whose snapshot products is null keeps the draft and the snapshot

mutations.because: toProduct writes inputAsset only when its trimmed value is non-empty, so canonicalProduct must drop null, "" and a blank string alike. Keeping an empty-string key makes a file carrying inputAsset: "" open dirty against its own snapshot.
command: a freshly opened brief with an empty-string product inputAsset is not dirty
